course_description:
Accounting involves compiling and interpreting financial information about an enterprise and its activities as a basis for making and evaluating economic decisions about the deployment of resources. Accounting knowledge is important for anyone involved in modern enterprises, whether they be profit oriented or government/non-profit entities. The aim of the course is to provide a broad understanding of the accounting discipline to enable students to comprehend, evaluate, interpret, question and intelligently discuss accounting information; and understand the uses, limitations, complexities and evolving nature of accounting. This broad understanding will enable students to make better decisions both when using accounting information and when working with their finance teams.

The course will equip you with the essential accounting knowledge you need as a manager or investor. It covers three key areas:

1. Measuring business activity

We explore how business transactions are recorded in the three financial statements, the Balance Sheet, Income Statement, and Cash Flow Statement, what they tell and how they are interconnected.

2. Analysing performance

In the second part of the course, we learn accounting techniques for analysing an organisation’s performance. First, we examine financial statements from an investor’s perspective using ratio analysis and learn about how to value a company. Then, we take a managerial perspective and analyse the costing of products and services, their profitability, the break-even point, and marginal costs.

3. Driving performance

In the final part of the course, we focus on driving performance to meet stakeholders’ objectives. We cover governance and ESG reporting requirements and discuss how to align incentives and how to encourage employees to achieve organisational goals.

Course Changes in Response to Previous Student Feedback

The course assessments have been updated to strengthen student engagement and enhance assessment integrity. The course follows a more scaffolded structure, ensuring that topics build progressively on prior concepts to support deeper learning.

assessment_details.task_description: You are required to work in groups to conduct a professional corporate analysis , focused on one ASX-listed company, comparing it with its key competitor(s) to evaluate its investment potential. The main tasks include: • Review, analyse and compare an entity to a listed entity • Make a recommendation of whether to invest in the company and why • Present and submit your analysis as a slide deck with speaker notes • Present live in-class and answer questions • All group members need to be prepared to answer questions This assessment is designed to develop the analytical, strategic, and communication capabilities expected of MBA graduates. It mirrors the type of corporate briefing delivered in consulting, investment analysis, and executive advisory contexts. Please Note: The presentation will be recorded for marking purposes per UQ Policy. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: A2: Forecasting and Financial Analysis
assessment_details.task_description: Your task is to develop five-year financial projections for a startup venture and to analyse the profitability outlook. For a startup venture that you develop, you are required to: Prepare projected 5-year proforma financial statements based on relevant assumptions Prepare a sensitivity analysis showing the impact of variations in your key assumptions Calculate financial ratios that demonstrate the financial health of the enterprise Prepare a cost–volume–profit (CVP) analysis for the enterprise Prepare a short-written report : Explaining how you determined which assumptions were most relevant and how you estimated the assumptions Analysing the breakeven and profitability outlook for the venture Discussing what the five-year outlook is for the venture, based on the most relevant financial data Approximate word count: 1,000 words Read full task description Hide full task description
